text:
Anaheim did most of the things that win hockey games on Wednesday. Justus Annunen made sure they didn't count. The Predators won 4-2 at Honda Center, their sixth straight win, and ended the Ducks' five-game winning streak in a game the Ducks deserved to win 69% of the time.

The gap in chances was real. Anaheim built 4.41 expected goals (the quality of chances) to Nashville's 3.11, with a big third period, 1.89 to 1.04. Annunen stopped 27 of 29 and saved 2.4 goals more than his shots deserved; his best stop, on Beckett Sennecke in the third, and a denial of Cutter Gauthier on a 25% look, kept the night from turning. Gauthier, the league's hottest scorer lately and the NHL's First Star of last week, put seven shots on goal and opened the scoring at 8:08 of the first. Nashville answered 21 seconds later through Jayden Struble.

The Predators' third line did the damage. Nils Hoglander's between-the-legs finish at 16:02 of the second made it 2-1 and pushed Nashville's win chance from 48% to 70%. Shane Wright then scored on a backhand at 8:05 of the third that had about a 2% chance of going in, the least likely goal of the night, to make it 3-1. Wright, acquired from Seattle for Matthew Wood on November 2, finished with a goal and two assists in 13 minutes. Mikael Granlund pulled Anaheim within one at 12:11, but Steven Stamkos restored the two-goal lead at 16:04, with Roman Josi picking up the second assist for his 800th career point.

Laurent Brossoit, who had won four straight, allowed four goals on 22 shots. Neither power play scored, though Anaheim's three chances produced 0.97 expected goals to Nashville's 0.18.

This is a different Nashville team from a month ago. The six-game run has come with Filip Forsberg out of his slump and Stamkos and Josi climbing record lists. Wednesday was not the cleanest of the six. It may be the one that tells you most about what a hot goalie can do for a team on a roll, and the Ducks can fairly feel they played well enough to keep their own streak going.
headline: Annunen steals one as Nashville makes it six
